premises.name: Sylow.exists_subgroup_card_pow_prime
premises.type: {G : Type u} [Group G] [Finite G] (p : ℕ) {n : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hdvd : p ^ n ∣ Nat.card G) : ∃ K, Nat.card ↥K = p ^ n
premises.doc:
A generalisation of **Sylow's first theorem**. If `p ^ n` divides
the cardinality of `G`, then there is a subgroup of cardinality `p ^ n`

premises.name: Sylow.exists_subgroup_card_pow_prime_of_le_card
premises.type: {G : Type u} [Group G] {n p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (h : IsPGroup p G) (hn : p ^ n ≤ Nat.card G) : ∃ H, Nat.card ↥H = p ^ n
premises.doc:
A special case of **Sylow's first theorem**. If `G` is a `p`-group of size at least `p ^ n`
then there is a subgroup of cardinality `p ^ n`.

premises.name: Sylow.exists_subgroup_le_card_pow_prime_of_le_card
premises.type: {G : Type u} [Group G] {n p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (h : IsPGroup p G) {H : Subgroup G} (hn : p ^ n ≤ Nat.card ↥H) : ∃ H' ≤ H, Nat.card ↥H' = p ^ n
premises.doc:
A special case of **Sylow's first theorem**. If `G` is a `p`-group and `H` a subgroup of size at
least `p ^ n` then there is a subgroup of `H` of cardinality `p ^ n`.

premises.name: Sylow.exists_subgroup_le_card_le
premises.type: {G : Type u} [Group G] {k p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (h : IsPGroup p G) {H : Subgroup G} (hk : k ≤ Nat.card ↥H) (hk₀ : k ≠ 0) : ∃ H' ≤ H, Nat.card ↥H' ≤ k ∧ k < p * Nat.card ↥H'
premises.doc:
A special case of **Sylow's first theorem**. If `G` is a `p`-group and `H` a subgroup of size at
least `k` then there is a subgroup of `H` of cardinality between `k / p` and `k`.

premises.name: Sylow.exists_subgroup_card_pow_prime_le
premises.type: {G : Type u} [Group G] [Finite G] (p : ℕ) {n m : ℕ} [_hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (_hdvd : p ^ m ∣ Nat.card G) (H : Subgroup G) (_hH : Nat.card ↥H = p ^ n) (_hnm : n ≤ m) : ∃ K, Nat.card ↥K = p ^ m ∧ H ≤ K
premises.doc:
If `H` is a subgroup of `G` of cardinality `p ^ n`,
then `H` is contained in a subgroup of cardinality `p ^ m`
if `n ≤ m` and `p ^ m` divides the cardinality of `G`

premises.name: Sylow.exists_subgroup_card_pow_succ
premises.type: {G : Type u} [Group G] [Finite G] {p n : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hdvd : p ^ (n + 1) ∣ Nat.card G) {H : Subgroup G} (hH : Nat.card ↥H = p ^ n) : ∃ K, Nat.card ↥K = p ^ (n + 1) ∧ H ≤ K
premises.doc:
If `H` is a subgroup of `G` of cardinality `p ^ n`,
then `H` is contained in a subgroup of cardinality `p ^ (n + 1)`
if `p ^ (n + 1)` divides the cardinality of `G`

premises.name: Sylow.prime_pow_dvd_card_normalizer
premises.type: {G : Type u} [Group G] [Finite G] {p n : ℕ} [_hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hdvd : p ^ (n + 1) ∣ Nat.card G) {H : Subgroup G} (hH : Nat.card ↥H = p ^ n) : p ^ (n + 1) ∣ Nat.card ↥(Subgroup.normalizer ↑H)
premises.doc:
If `H` is a `p`-subgroup but not a Sylow `p`-subgroup of cardinality `p ^ n`,
then `p ^ (n + 1)` divides the cardinality of the normalizer of `H`.

premises.name: Sylow.prime_dvd_card_quotient_normalizer
premises.type: {G : Type u} [Group G] [Finite G] {p n : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hdvd : p ^ (n + 1) ∣ Nat.card G) {H : Subgroup G} (hH : Nat.card ↥H = p ^ n) : p ∣ Nat.card (↥(Subgroup.normalizer ↑H) ⧸ Subgroup.comap (Subgroup.normalizer ↑H).subtype H)
premises.doc:
If `H` is a `p`-subgroup but not a Sylow `p`-subgroup, then `p` divides the
index of `H` inside its normalizer.

premises.name: Sylow.exists_orderEmbedding
premises.type: {G : Type u} [Group G] [Finite G] {p n : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (h : p ^ n ∣ Nat.card G) : ∃ f, ∀ (k : Fin (n + 1)), Nat.card ↥(f k) = p ^ ↑k
premises.doc:
A corollary of **Sylow's first theorem**. If `p ^ n` divides the order of the group, then
there is a tower of subgroups of orders `p ^ 0, …, p ^ n`.

premises.name: Sylow.exists_orderEmbedding_of_isChain
premises.type: {G : Type u} [Group G] [Finite G] {p n : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hdvd : p ^ n ∣ Nat.card G) {s : Set (Subgroup G)} (hchain : IsChain (fun x1 x2 => x1 ≤ x2) s) (hcard : ∀ H ∈ s, Nat.card ↥H ∣ p ^ n) : ∃ f, s ⊆ Set.range ⇑f ∧ ∀ (k : Fin (n + 1)), Nat.card ↥(f k) = p ^ ↑k
premises.doc:
A corollary of **Sylow's first theorem**. If `p ^ n` divides the order of `G`, then any chain
of subgroups whose orders divide `p ^ n` can be completed to a tower of subgroups of orders
`p ^ 0, …, p ^ n`.
